news.headline: Orangutans released back into Borneo forest after devastating fires
news.story_lead: Watch: Endangered orangutans released back into the wild after after Borneo fires - Published 5 hours ago Eight orangutans have been released back into the wild in Borneo after they were taken into captivity when their habitat was threatened by wildfires over the summer. Three mothers, their three daughters and two adult males were freed in a reserve in the west of the island on Friday, International Animal Rescue Indonesia (Yiari) and the forestry ministry said. Indonesian authorities rescued 46 orangutans from fires in August and September.
news.full_article_text: Watch: Endangered orangutans released back into the wild after after Borneo fires - Published 5 hours ago Eight orangutans have been released back into the wild in Borneo after they were taken into captivity when their habitat was threatened by wildfires over the summer. Three mothers, their three daughters and two adult males were freed in a reserve in the west of the island on Friday, International Animal Rescue Indonesia (Yiari) and the forestry ministry said. Indonesian authorities rescued 46 orangutans from fires in August and September. Wildfires in the region are usual for the country's dry season but intensified this year. The apes are critically endangered. Around 104,000 orangutans remain in Borneo and Sumatra, down from more than 230,000 a century ago, according to conservation group WWF. While Indonesia is among many countries to grapple with wildfires each summer, this year's were more intense due to the El NiÃ±o ocean warming phenomenon, which makes weather patterns more volatile and intense. Yiari CEO Karmele Llano Sanchez said relocating the eight orangutans to the reserve was a "necessary step" when their habitats became unsafe. Among them was Mama Nopi and her offspring Nopi, Naufal and Nopan, who had been surviving in a coconut and rubber plantation before their rescue in early September, Yiari said. Fires had incinerated the surrounding forestry, restricting their access to food and bringing them closer to humans. The apes were all rescued from wildfires over the summer that threatened their habitats Mama Lifa and her child Lifa were found in a patch of acacia trees entirely surrounded by oil palm plantations. The degradation of their habitat by wildfires as well as a lack of food sources prompted their rescue in mid-September. Mama Man and her baby, Man, had been monitored by animal rescuers since June, when they were found living in a plantation area adjacent to a small patch of forest. Fires that spread near to the site restricted their roaming area further, leaving them without a safe route to other forestry. The threat of exposure to the blazes led to them being evacuated in early September, Yiara said. The reserve these orangutans were released into was chosen because it there is food and water available and it is connected to other forested areas. Yiari's Argitoe Ranting said: "We want to ensure that rescued orangutans are not simply moved from one place to another, but actually have a chance to survive in their natural habitat." The orangutans were moved to a reserve connected with other forests and with plenty of natural resources Last month, the International Union for Conservation of Nature warned that wildfires were burning in habitats containing 52% of Borneo's orangutan population. It says a large portion of the ape's habitat will become inhospitable to them if climate change continues at its current pace. This year's El NiÃ±o has become the strongest on record and is expected to have a knock-on effect on the climate into next year. Experts have also pointed to land-clearing practices used to make room for plantations as another factor facilitating the spread of wildfires in Indonesia, with naturally fire-resistant forests replaced by less dense and shaded vegetation. That the orangutan's original habitats had been burned and fragmented to the point they could no longer sustain the primates was the main driving factor behind relocating them, Yiara said. news.headline: Sachin Pilot may even deny me ticket; will always remain Rahul Gandhi’s soldier: Warring
news.story_lead: Sachin Pilot may even deny me ticket; will always remain Rahul Gandhi’s soldier: Warring Warring quit as the Punjab Congress chief on October 1, after the Congress high command decided on a leadership change ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Days after quitting as the Punjab Congress president, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Sunday said he may have "lost or fallen", or AICC's Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot may even deny him a ticket for next year's Assembly elections, yet he would continue to hold the Congress flag high as a soldier of Rahul Gandhi. The Ludhiana MP also acknowledged that many in the party opposed him when he was the Punjab Congress president, and that they may continue to do so – remarks seen as directed at his detractors in the state unit.
news.full_article_text: Sachin Pilot may even deny me ticket; will always remain Rahul Gandhi’s soldier: Warring Warring quit as the Punjab Congress chief on October 1, after the Congress high command decided on a leadership change ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Days after quitting as the Punjab Congress president, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Sunday said he may have "lost or fallen", or AICC's Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot may even deny him a ticket for next year's Assembly elections, yet he would continue to hold the Congress flag high as a soldier of Rahul Gandhi. The Ludhiana MP also acknowledged that many in the party opposed him when he was the Punjab Congress president, and that they may continue to do so – remarks seen as directed at his detractors in the state unit. Warring, however, said he will fully support new Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh, who on Sunday took charge of his new post at a ceremony held at the Congress Bhavan that was attended by Pilot, among others. Ahead of the ceremony, Warring held a gathering at a rented house in Sector 10, close to the party headquarters in Sector 15, where Congress leaders Brahm Mohindra, Rana K P Singh, Surinder Dawar, Anil Joshi, Simarjit Singh Bains, Hardyal Kamboj, Malvika Sood and his supporters were present. The gathering was seen as a show of strength by Warring. Amid an intense race for the top organisational post, with former Sangrur MP Vijay Inder Singla seen as a frontrunner, the party named ex-India hockey captain and three-time Jalandhar Cantt MLA Pargat Singh (61) as the new state unit chief the next day. The move followed weeks of internal unrest over the state leadership that threatened to hurt the party's campaign for the Assembly elections due early next year. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Warring said the Congress is united in its quest to form the next government in Punjab. "There is no other objective. Raja Warring may have lost and fallen, but my job is to keep holding the party flag high," Warring said. Later during his address at the Congress Bhavan with Pilot in attendance, Warring stressed that he was a soldier of Rahul Gandhi. "No doubt many people opposed Raja Warring, and they may continue to do so. But I am not opposing anyone," he said. Hinting at his resignation, Warring said Pilot was here and "I myself had said I have lost". "I only consider Rahul Gandhi as my leader," he said, adding that the Congress gave a lot to him. "If I say that I would remain the president and only what I say should be heard, it won't be right," Warring said. In an apparent dig at Pilot, Warring said, "Pilot Saab may cut my ticket next time. But I will continue to remain a soldier of Rahul Gandhi and will always be with the Congress." After the party decided to replace him on October 2, Warring had said he came to know that Pilot wanted him replaced, but he "voluntarily" relinquished his charge. On Sunday, Warring said he would continue to support whoever the party makes the president. Referring to his recent meeting with Rahul Gandhi, Warring said he urged the senior party leader to allot more than 50 per cent tickets to the youth fighting the party's battle. Before the ceremony, Warring said, "I had maintained that whosoever becomes the (Punjab Congress) president, I would be with him. Be it Pargat Singh or Charanjit Singh Channi." However, he added that Channi did not want to go along with him. Warring was replaced as the Punjab Congress chief weeks after Pilot took charge as the general secretary in charge of Punjab. A section of leaders led by Channi had opposed a move to retain Warring as the state unit president and sought his removal from the post.

BJP leader Kirit Somaiya has urged the Mumbai Police to take action against actor Imran Khan for joining a protest in support of the Cockroach Janta Party, citing his alleged status as a “foreign citizen”. Calling for Khan's detention and deportation, the BJP leader also sought clarity on whether the actor could participate in such protests. In a post on X, Somaiya said he had written to Mumbai Police Joint Commissioner Manoj Kumar Sharma, asking whether Khan, a “foreign citizen”, could “break the law knowingly”. Somaiya called for Khan to be charged for participating in what he described as an illegal political agitation, alleging violations of OCI provisions and visa conditions. He argued that foreign citizens do not enjoy the same rights as Indian citizens. Deep Dive He also demanded Khan’s immediate deportation. Khan was detained by the Mumbai Police on October 10 from Mumbai's August Kranti Maidan, which was the proposed protest venue in support of CJP’s protest call. news.full_article_text: CJI Surya Kant declines Opposition leaders' request for meet over SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar; cites judicial propriety The Opposition’s proposed intervention also comes amid its continuing campaign against the SIR exercise and allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls. The Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has declined a request by Opposition leaders to meet him on Monday, citing extensive reasons why such an interaction would not be appropriate at this juncture and in the present circumstances, dealing a setback to the Opposition’s plan to seek his intervention over the crackdown on a youth-led protest in Delhi and alleged irregularities in electoral processes. Among the key reasons cited were the pendency of related matters before the Supreme Court in its judicial capacity and the CJI’s own adjudicatory role in petitions concerning these issues, people aware of the matter said. Also Read | Opposition march to Supreme Court tomorrow; leaders seek to meet CJI against SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar Opposition's meeting with CJI Deep Dive The decision came hours after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi announced that they had sought time to meet the CJI between 4 pm and 5 pm on Monday. Kharge had said that he and Gandhi had written to the CJI, seeking an opportunity to apprise him of their concerns over the functioning of constitutional institutions and request his intervention. The Opposition had planned to raise several issues, including the police action against protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the expeditious hearing of cases concerning the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and the composition of the committee that recommends appointments to the Election Commission. The proposed meeting had not been confirmed by the CJI’s office when the Opposition announced its plans on Sunday. Kharge, speaking to reporters in Bengaluru, had said the delegation would place its concerns before the CJI with folded hands, adding that the leaders could not make demands of the head of the judiciary. Also Read | After CJP, Opposition calls for protest, march to Supreme Court to demand action against SIR “We have scheduled a meeting between 4 and 5 pm, during which we will apprise him (CJI) of the situation. We cannot demand anything from him, but we will place our concerns before him with folded hands and request his intervention,” Kharge had said. Protests in Delhi The CJI’s refusal comes against the backdrop of four days of Opposition demonstrations in Delhi, including protests near the Election Commission of India (ECI), a sit-in at Rajghat and an attempt to march to the poll panel’s office. Opposition leaders had also met President Droupadi Murmu to raise their concerns over the Election Commission’s functioning and alleged electoral irregularities. Kharge on Sunday accused the Narendra Modi-led government of imposing an “undeclared Emergency” in the country, alleging that the heavy police deployment and detention of protesters reflected an attempt to suppress dissent. “The Prime Minister and the Home Minister have created chaos across the country. An undeclared Emergency is prevailing, and we will continue to fight against it. We will continue our fight to protect democracy and the constitutional rights of the people,” he said. March towards Supreme Court on Monday Rahul Gandhi had separately announced a march towards the Supreme Court on Monday, calling on Opposition parties, young people and civil society groups to join the protest. He alleged that young people who had taken part in a peaceful demonstration in Delhi on Saturday were beaten by police and BJP supporters. “Tomorrow, we will march to the Supreme Court as Indians, united beyond party, gender, caste, community and state. Youth, all opposition parties, civil society groups, all those who believe in democracy and stand by the Constitution of India, will walk with us,” Gandhi said. Also Read | Opposition panel meets President Murmu, Rahul Gandhi says ‘vote chori’ proof sought He had said the march would culminate in the submission of a memorandum to the CJI, seeking an end to alleged “vote chori”, the halting of SIR and the removal of Gyanesh Kumar as chief election commissioner. Gandhi also accused the government of attempting to intimidate those raising questions about electoral processes. CJI’s inclusion in committee selecting election commissioners The demand for the CJI’s inclusion in the committee selecting election commissioners is linked to a pending challenge to the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. Under the law, the selection committee comprises the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister. The 2023 law replaced an earlier arrangement laid down by the Supreme Court, under which the CJI was part of the selection committee until Parliament enacted a law governing appointments. The Opposition has argued that excluding the CJI undermines the independence of the Election Commission. On September 23, a bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma delivered a split verdict on whether the challenge to the 2023 law should be referred to a Constitution bench. Justice Datta held that such a reference was unnecessary because the challenge could be decided on the basis of settled principles laid down in earlier judgments. Justice Sharma, however, favoured a five-judge bench, holding that the case raised substantial questions concerning the interpretation of the Constitution. The Opposition’s proposed intervention also comes amid its continuing campaign against the SIR exercise and allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls. The Election Commission and the BJP have rejected allegations of deliberate manipulation of voter lists, maintaining that deletions during revision exercises can arise from factors such as deaths, migration and voters being untraceable. Former Chhattisgarh chief minister and Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel had said that party MPs, MLAs and district presidents would travel to Delhi for Monday’s march. He alleged that the public mandate had been stolen through manipulation of electronic voting machines in some places and the removal of names from electoral rolls in others. The Opposition’s efforts to escalate its campaign have drawn a mixed response from parties over the role of the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), whose supporters have been at the centre of the recent protests. news.full_article_text: Maharashtra govt to submit detailed memorandum for Central drought relief Mumbai, Oct 11 Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday said the state government is undertaking detailed planning to provide employment, foodgrains, drinking water and fodder for livestock in drought-affected areas over the next six to eight months. At a meeting with a Central drought assessment team at his official residence here, Fadnavis said deficient rainfall during a crucial stage of crop growth had severely affected soybean cultivation in several areas, while cotton, tur and sugarcane crops had also suffered damage. The prospects for rabi sowing are bleak due to water shortages, leaving farmers with little scope to make up for their kharif crop losses through subsequent cultivation, he said. Small farmers dependent on agricultural labour for livelihood are facing economic hardship, and the government will provide assistance through employment generation and food security schemes, Fadnavis said. He expressed confidence that the Central team, which visited drought-affected villages and interacted with farmers, would submit a report highlighting the severity of the situation to the Union government. "Water sources have dried up in several parts of Maharashtra, particularly in small rural villages, necessitating extensive arrangements for tanker-based supply. The state government is planning to use technology to ensure transparent and systematic distribution of water through tankers," he said. Fadnavis said drinking water requirements of people and livestock will be prioritised, with available water reserved for drinking purposes until August 2027. Water for other uses would be made available only after these requirements were met, he added. "The government will also undertake desilting, repairs and rejuvenation of water storage structures under various Central and state schemes. Works in 25,000 villages had earlier provided relief even when the water deficit was between 15 and 17 per cent," Fadnavis said, adding that software and mobile applications would be used to ensure transparency in implementation. The available fodder stock in various districts is estimated to last 90 to 120 days, the chief minister said, adding that production will be increased in watershed areas with adequate soil moisture. He said the government would procure fodder at declared rates and arrange for its storage. "Procurement from other states with better rainfall would also be considered if necessary," he said, adding that fodder and cattle camps will be set up wherever required, while water conservation works will be undertaken with public participation to generate employment in rural areas. He said the state government will submit a detailed memorandum, supported by data and prepared in accordance with the Union government's norms, to seek drought relief. "An advance memorandum had already been submitted following communication from the Union Agriculture Minister," Fadnavis said. He added that the Union Home Minister had assured the state that a meeting of an inter-ministerial group would be convened soon to expedite the relief process. The state government will also coordinate with the Centre to ensure that farmers covered by crop insurance received their benefits at the earliest, he said. The meeting was attended by Disaster Management Minister Girish Mahajan, Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharne, Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Makarand Jadhav Patil, and Central team head and Joint Secretary Muktanand Agrawal, among others. Three teams of Central government officials visited agricultural fields and water sources in drought-affected villages across Ahilyanagar, Solapur, Jalna, Beed, Dharashiv, Washim and Yavatmal districts to assess the situation and interact with farmers.
